b.e39ef74ff2:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>I</c>n cælesti collégio
Novus colléga colitur:
In sanctórum rosário
Novéllus flos producitur.

<h>F</h>ranciscus florens grátia,
Forma factus humilium,
Lætus potitur glória,
Sortis consors sublimium.

<h>M</h>etit de sparso sémine
Plenæ messis manípulum,
Fallens sub terræ tegmine
Nostræ salutis æmulum.

<h>H</h>ic carnis supercilium
Legi subjêcit spiritus:
Mundum vicit et vitium,
Se victo victor inclitus.

<h>L</h>inguæ manus præámbula
Verbo parávit sémitam:
Et amplectúntur sæcula
Doctrinam facto próditam.

<h>I</h>n paupertatis prædio
Minórum plantans víneam,
Osténdit, magistério
Vitæ, vivéndi líneam.

<h>A</h>d ætérnas divitias
Turbam alléxit páuperum,
Quos ad cæli delicias
Lingua vocávit óperum.

<h>V</h>ita, doctrina splénduit,
Respléndet et miraculis:
Sic præfuit, quod prófuit,
Viva lucérna pópulis.

<h>S</h>ummi Regis palátio
Doctor loca discíulos:
Salútis privilégio
Christi præmúni fámulos.

<h>D</h>e ténebris misériæ,
Sequáces stellæ præviæ,
Quærámus Patrem grátia,
Consórtes tandem glóriæ.
Amen.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
De Epistola beáti Pauli Apóstoli ad Gálatas
<r>Gal 5:25-26; 6:1-6</r>
<n>25</n> Si Spíritu vívimus, spíritu et ambulemus.
<n>26</n> Non efficiámur inánis glóriæ cúpidi, invicem provocántes, invicem invidéntes.
<n>1</n> Fratres, etsi præoccupátus fúerit homo in aliquo delícto, vos, qui spirituales estis, hujusmodi instrúite in spíritu lenitátis consíderans te ipsum, ne et tu tenteris.
<n>2</n> Alter alterius onera portate, et sic adimplébitis legem Christi.
<n>3</n> Nam, si quis existimat se aliquid esse, cum nihil sit, ipse se sedúcit.
<n>4</n> Opus autem suum probet unusquísque, et sic in semetípso tantum glóriam habébit et non in altero.
<n>5</n> Unusquisque enim onus suum portabit.
<n>6</n> Communicet autem is qui catechizátur verbo, ei qui se catechízat in ómnibus bonis.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

* Invéntum evangélicum thesárum vult mercári.

<r>℟.</r> Invéntum evangélicum thesárum vult mercári.

<h>Reading 1</h>
From the letter of St. Paul to the Galatians.
<r>Gal 5:25-26; 6:1-6</r>
<n>25</n> If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit.
<n>26</n> Let us not be made desirous of vain glory, provoking one another, envying on another.
<n>1</n> Brethren, and if a man be overtaken in any fault, you, who are spiritual, instruct such a one in the spirit of meekness, considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.
<n>2</n> Bear ye one another's burdens; and so you shall fulfil the law of Christ.
<n>3</n> For if any man think himself to be some thing, whereas he is nothing, he deceiveth himself.
<n>4</n> But let every one prove his own work, and so he shall have glory in himself only, and not in another.
<n>5</n> For every one shall bear his own burden.
<n>6</n> And let him that is instructed in the word, communicate to him that instructeth him, in all good things.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>Gal 6:7-13</r>
<n>7</n> Nolíte errare: Deus non irridétur.
<n>8</n> Quæ enim seminaverit homo hæc et metet. Quóniam qui seminat in carne sua, de carne et metet corruptiónem; qui autem seminat in spiritu, de spíritu metet vitam ætérnam.
<n>9</n> Bonum autem faciéntes non deficiámus; témpore enim suo metémus non deficiéntes.
<n>10</n> Ergo, dum tempus habemus, operemur bonum ad omnes, maxime autem ad domesticos fidei.
<n>11</n> Vidéte quálibus litteris scripsi vobis mea manu.
<n>12</n> Quicúmque enim volunt placére in carne, hi cogunt vos circumcidi, tantum ut crucis Christi persecutiónem non patiántur.
<n>13</n> Neque enim qui circumcidúntur, legem custódiunt; sed volunt vos circumcidi, ut in carne vestra glorientur.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<c>G</c>al 6:7-13
<n>7</n> Be not deceived, God is not mocked.

<c>O</c>ctober 5th 2027, the 5th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Messina, in Sicily, (in the year 546,) the holy monk Placidus, a disciple of the blessed Abbot Benedict, his brothers Eutychius and Victorinus, and the Virgin Flavia, their sister, along with Donatus, the Deacon Firmatus, Faustus, and thirty other monks, all martyrs, who were massacred for Christ's faith's sake, by the pirate Manucha.
<h>U</h>pon the same day, (in the year 171,) blessed Thraseas, Bishop of Eumenia, who achieved his martyrdom at Smyrna.
<h>A</h>t Auxerre, the holy Deacon Firmatus, (in the fifth or sixth century,) and the Virgin Flaviana his sister.
<h>A</h>t Trier, the holy martyrs Palmatius and his Companions, who underwent martyrdom under the President Rictiovarus, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.
<h>O</h>n the same day, the holy Virgin Charitina, under the Emperor Diocletian and the Consular Domitius. She was tormented with fire, and cast into the sea, whence she came forth unharmed, then her hands and feet were cut off, and her teeth shaken, and she gave up her soul in prayer to God.
<h>A</h>t Ravenna, the holy Confessor Marcellinus, Bishop of (that see.)
<h>A</h>t Valence, in Gaul, holy Apollinaris, (about the year 520,) Bishop (of that see) his life was famous for his graces, and his death was marked by signs and wonders.
<h>U</h>pon the same day holy Attilan, Bishop of Zamora, whose name Urban II. numbered with those of the Saints.
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy widow Galla, daughter of the Consul Symmachus after the death of her husband she passed many years at the church of blessed Peter, intent upon prayer, alms, fastings, and other holy works. Holy Pope Gregory hath written of her right blessed passage hence.
